note: HKEX/SGX activity proxy for the trough-quarter roll-off is offset by the FX line that drove the last -18.9% print; the two cancel on a $10k/day name whose real earnings reactions are far wider than the 1.5% cadence-polluted median.

Three end-market proxies (record July heat into GTV, JOLTS trades hiring into seats, Watsco vs Lennox) all lean positive but none is a company number and all sit against a 5-point paid downside skew, so each is sized small.

Irenic's search-invisible 5.41% activist stake, read into the story on results morning with EQT's Rule 2.8 restriction expired, carries the number; the unpublished H1 EBITDA/one-offs and Vulpes' distribution cut it back on a name that has only ever sold its scheduled releases.

Run-rate arithmetic from the company's own releases puts Q4 revenue above where the two-analyst consensus sits, into a 25%-of-float short with 49 days to cover; the pattern of declining to guide and the December covenant snapback are the negatives.

The CFO named memory cost as the gross-margin risk in June and the DRAM squeeze has since escalated, on a name that falls on 5 of 7 prints and has rallied 13% into this one on no corporate bid (dormant buyback, Point72 gone); the ITC exit is the only positive.

The +88% RPO footnote gives guidance headroom the consumption-only re-rating ignores, but it reads through to total revenue rather than Atlas and the stock is up 23% in 20 days; the CRO handover quarter is a modest offset that Citizens' channel work argues against.

CAAC's actual July volumes and double-digit holiday forward bookings refute the syndicated -3.6% projection, but hotel ADR deflation lands on the accommodation take-rate and the last guide-down cost 12.5%, so the two nearly offset at a fresh 52-week low.

The FY27 guide needs a four-point revenue inflection starting in the quarter being reported, from a company that flagged government softness and a Q1 at -4.7%, with a new CFO owning the number for the first time; a refinancing statement is a wide two-sided branch and sized near zero.

A 9%-of-float unregistered Cipher block out of lock-up since 23 August, held by a seller that has written it down and needs cash, into a 68% rally built on a buyback that has executed 6.7% of its authorisation, plus a halved mining run-rate hidden by a paused-but-counted Ethiopian fleet.

The 10-Q covenant mechanics (26% revolver usage below the 35% test trigger, 3.3x against a 4.0x maximum) remove the credit tail the 6-point put skew is paying for, and officer grants keyed to H2 comp growth made 27 days after quarter close argue against a withdrawn year; the World Cup peer read is two-sided for a sports bar.

A third shift being staffed end-to-end at Torrington is a real ramp tell and a new director bought $495k in the open market, but both sit against the strongest put skew in the pack (11.6 points) and a Fit Energy deal whose only alignment warrants are 58% out of the money with no phase election, so the print as a whole is a coin flip.

RPO fell $36m sequentially last quarter (book-to-bill ~0.6) and no large booking was announced in the quarter now reported, while FY27 EBITDA is guided below FY26 actual under a 'path to breakeven' framing; on-time Pelican launches and BlackSky's strong print are the offset on a name that moves 20%+.

NICS accelerated 5 points into the fiscal quarter and two direct suppliers (Ruger sell-through +19%, Winchester +11.8%) confirmed it after the company last spoke, with the three estimates unmoved and no peer printing first; the 32.0% gross-margin lap and firearms mix dilution are why a top-line beat is sized net rather than gross (hunter b's items 14-16 merged into 0 and 2 as duplicates).
